attachments.origin_landmark: submucous fibrous layer near the epiglottis and the median septum
attachments.insertion_landmark: mucosa at the tip and margins of the tongue

actions: turns the tip and sides upwards, making the dorsum concave

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: A single sheet directly beneath the dorsal mucosa, the most superficial of the intrinsic muscles.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Not an ultrasound-guided technique -- injected directly, via an intraoral needle approach from the dorsum of the tongue, under EMG guidance. Used bilaterally, in two or three sites, for the curling-up subtype of lingual dystonia, and as an adjunct near the apex for tongue-tip curling; also used unilaterally to counteract protrusion accompanied by curling-up.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Approximately 5 mm depth from the dorsal mucosa, consistent with this being the most superficial intrinsic tongue muscle, lying directly beneath the dorsal mucosa.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: EMG confirmation of recruitment during the dystonic curling-up movement, including near the tongue apex if apex curling is present.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Only described as one component of an individualized, EMG-mapped injection plan for lingual dystonia (curling type showed the greatest overall improvement of the four described subtypes, though the difference from other subtypes was not statistically significant), not as a standalone BoNT indication. Reported dose for the curling subtype: 10-40 U across the targeted muscles.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Yoshida K, 'Botulinum Neurotoxin Therapy for Lingual Dystonia Using an Individualized Injection Method Based on Clinical Features', Toxins (Basel) 11(1):51 (2019), doi:10.3390/toxins11010051 -- retrieved via PubMed.
